newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.S. party opposes $1.75 billion green bond act.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.S. party opposes $1.75 billion green bond act.

text.p: New York State Conservative Party said Monday it opposed a $1.75 billion environmental bond act proposed by Gov. George Pataki to clean up the state's air, water and land.

The party, which with 148,000 members is the state's third largest after the Republican and the Democratic parties, echoed some of the criticisms articulated by a taxpayers' association, CHANGE-NY, and the Assembly Majority Leader.

Michael Bragman, D-Syracuse, has submitted an alternative bill, which uses a "pay-as-you-go" approach, to the proposed $1.75 billion bond act, which the voters will accept or reject at the Nov 5 elections.

Saying it preferred the pay-as-you-go approach to having to pay $1 billion in interest that would be due with the bond act, Michael Long, the conservatives' chairman, said "This bond issue will not improve the environment but it will set New York State back on the irresponsible track of unnecessary borrowing and wasteful spending." His comments were released in a prepared statement.

However, a spokesman for the campaign for the bond act said experience has shown that using a pay-as-you-go strategy does not work. He noted that this method would raise far less than the $900 million that would be spent in the first five years of the bond act.

As a result, a number of projects, which have been waiting for funds, would be delayed, making their eventual clean-up much more costly. "Pay-as-you-go is cleary insufficient to meet the state's environmental needs. There is no certainity to it," the spokesman said.
The opponents of the bond act also have faulted it for including a variety of so-called questionable projects, including land purchases, parking lots and zoos.

A spokesman for the campaign for the bond act countered such criticisms by saying they only represent two to three percent of the bond act. He added there are adequate safeguards to ensure only needed projects, like roads for water treatment plants are built, or zoos that meet the criteria for historic preservation, get funds.
